candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 17:1-13. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Tewahedo Marian liturgical witness: Wǝddase Maryam (Praises of Mary).
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On Aaron's rod that 'budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds' (Num 17:8), Ephrem reads the blossoming-of-the-dead-staff as the canonical Marian-rod typology: a dry rod brings forth life out of season because the Lord wills it, prefiguring the Virgin who bears the Word without seed. The Tewahedo Wǝddase Maryam preserves this reading explicitly — Mary is the 'rod of Aaron' (in Geʿez: bä-ṭwāf zä-Aron) whose blossoming is the seedless Conception of the Word. Num 17:8 is therefore the canonical Old-Testament Marian-iconographic anchor in Ethiopian devotion, alongside the burning bush (Ex 3:2) and the ladder of Jacob (Gen 28:12 + Jub 27:19).
